header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH BENCH AT SUKKUR
[Mst. Naghma v. P.O Sindh and others]
For Petitioner : Mr. Badaruddin Memon, Advocate
For Respondents : M/s Ali Raza Balouch & Israr Ahmed
body: Andan Iqbal Chaudhry J.- The grievance of the petitioner is that she has been denied appointment as Lady Police Constable on the ground that upon the medical screening test held during the recruitment process, she was detected with the Hepatitis “C” virus. Pursuant to the order dated 28.08.2024, passed in this petition she was retested from another medical lab, but again she tested „reactive‟ for the same virus. This fact is recorded in the order dated 10.10.2024.

Learned counsel for the petitioner yet again prays for another medical screening test. On the other hand, the learned AAG Sindh draws attention to clause 4.1.12 of the Police Recruitment Policy 2022, as amended vide letter dated 24.01.2025, which reads as follows:- 4.1.12 SCREENING OF QUALTIFIED CANDIDATES FOR HEPATITS “This screening should preferably be arranged through third party service provider but final decision lies with SPRB. All candidates who were detected with hepatitis “B” on the date of laboratory test will be disqualified for appointed as ASI, HC (Wireless Operator), PC, Driver PC, Ministerial, & Class-IV posts. Similarly all candidates who are detected (ELISA or ICT Test) as Reactive will be disqualified for appointment as ASI, HC (Wireless Operator), PC, Driver PC, Ministerial & Class-IV Posts. Their qualitative test Hepatitis “C” as PCR negative will not make them eligible for appointment because such candidates cannot performed strenuous long hours duty for Police Department and there are chances reactivation of Hepatitis “C”.

In our view, clause 4.1.12 assigns a plausible reason for not appointing persons who are reactive to Hepatitis ”C”. In any case, Page 2 of 2 the recruitment process for the year 2024, has since been completed. We are not inclined to re-open the same for that would be discrimination with candidates who were rejected for the same reason. However, as and when the petitioner is cured from the virus, and provided there is a vacancy, she will be free to apply afresh. With that observation, the petition is dismissed. J U D G E J U D G E M.Ali*
